items.title: An Understandable Response to a Terrible Loss
items.answer: Jeremiah felt the loss deeply, writing: "My eyes are worn out from shedding tears. My insides are churning." (La 2:11) Even amid judgment he urged Zion: "Pour out your heart like water before the face of Jehovah." (La 2:19) If we blame ourselves for the poor decisions of others, remember: each person answers for his own choices; even Jeremiah could not force anyone to return. Like him, we keep the door open, keep praying for the person, keep expressing confidence they can return, and leave the outcome with our merciful God.

scriptures.quote: My eyes are worn out from shedding tears. My insides are churning. My liver has been poured out on the ground, because of the downfall of the daughter of my people, Because of the children and infants fainting away in the public squares of the town.

Rise up! Cry out during the night, at the start of the watches. Pour out your heart like water before the face of Jehovah. Raise your hands to him for the lives of your children, Who are fainting away at every street corner because of famine.

items.cite: w24.08 28 pars. 7-9; FOR MEDITATION: w23.08 29-30 pars. 12-13

items.title: Spiritual Gems
items.answer:
What I learned from this week's Bible reading (Lamentations 1-2):

1. Jehovah feels deeply for his people even while correcting them. Jeremiah's words at Lamentations 2:11 show a heart moved by other people's pain: "My eyes are worn out from shedding tears. My insides are churning. My liver has been poured out on the ground, because of the downfall of the daughter of my people, …" If Jehovah's servants feel that way, how much more does Jehovah himself? He does not enjoy seeing us suffer — he wants us to return to him.

2. Honest self-assessment brings us closer to Jehovah. Jerusalem finally admitted: "Jehovah is righteous, for it is against his commands that I have rebelled." (La 1:18) Owning our mistakes instead of making excuses is the first step back to God.

3. When we are at our lowest, prayer is the way out. "Pour out your heart like water before the face of Jehovah. Raise your hands to him for the lives of your children, …" (La 2:19) — said at night, at the start of the watches. Jehovah is never asleep and never too busy.

Practical examples from these scriptures — how they have helped, or can help:
• La 2:19 helped me personally: after a disappointment I had kept chewing over alone, I finally prayed specifically about it, at night, in my own words — like pouring out a bucket of water, nothing held back. The relief was real the next morning.
• La 1:18 can help in family life: when there is tension at home, saying sincerely "I was wrong about this" — instead of listing the other person's faults — often ends the argument on the spot.
• La 2:11 can help us comfort others: when a brother loses a job or a loved one, our first move should be to sit with him and feel his pain with him, not to rush in with explanations about why it happened.
• And La 2:1 — "How the beauty of Israel has been thrown down" — reminds us how quickly what looks secure can collapse when Jehovah's blessing is gone. It helps me keep spiritual things first, not 'when things settle down'.

scriptures.quote: My eyes are worn out from shedding tears. My insides are churning. My liver has been poured out on the ground, because of the downfall of the daughter of my people
Jehovah is righteous, for it is against his commands that I have rebelled
Rise up! Cry out during the night, at the start of the watches. Pour out your heart like water before the face of Jehovah. Raise your hands to him for the lives of your children

items.title: Bible Reading — La 1:8-18 (th study 10)
items.answer:
Context: Jerusalem laments the consequences of her own great sin—exile, hunger, the desecration of the temple—with no one to comfort her.

Lesson 1: Sin has consequences that touch even the things we treasure most (La 1:10). Lesson 2: Like Jerusalem, we do well to admit our error to Jehovah rather than make excuses (La 1:18).

Possible comment: "Jerusalem has sinned greatly. That is why she has become something abhorrent." (La 1:8) Jerusalem's fall came from her own choices, not from bad luck. That helps me guard my heart today, because the same principle holds: walking with Jehovah brings security, while drifting from him always costs more than we expect.

scriptures.quote: Jerusalem has sinned greatly. That is why she has become something abhorrent. All who used to honor her now treat her as something contemptible, for they have seen her nakedness. She herself groans and turns away in shame.

items.title: Starting a Conversation — Informal Witnessing (lmd lesson 2 point 4)
items.answer:
lmd lesson 2 point 4 — “Be patient. Do not feel that you must introduce a Bible truth immediately. Wait for the right opportunity so that you can bring it up naturally. Sometimes, this may mean waiting until the next conversation you have with the person.”

INFORMAL WITNESSING — Daniel starts a friendly conversation and, following the point, holds back from giving a witness because the right opportunity has not come yet. The conversation ends naturally before any witness, with the plan to bring up the truth on the next call.

Daniel (Publisher): "Good morning! Sorry — you must be the new neighbours? I'm Daniel, we're at number 12, just behind you."
Ruth (Householder): "Oh, good morning! Yes, we moved in last week. I'm Ama."
Daniel (Publisher): "Welcome to the neighbourhood, Ama. Ah — is this your little boy? He looks curious about everything this morning."
Ruth (Householder): "Ha! Yes, that one never stops. Three years old."
Daniel (Publisher): "Three — such a fun age. And you're settling in well? How are you finding the area?"
Ruth (Householder): "We're managing. I still don't know the place like that. The market, the school — I'm still finding my way around."
Daniel (Publisher): "You'll soon know every corner. If it helps, I can point you to the clinic, the nearest tro-tro stop, places like that — anything around here, feel free to ask me."
Ruth (Householder): "Oh thank you! I'll remember that."
Daniel (Publisher): "No problem at all. Ama, it was really nice meeting you — I'll let you carry on with your morning. Have a good day!"

Keys: Daniel follows lmd lesson 2 point 4 — he does not force a Bible truth in. Ama mentioned settling in, not spiritual matters, so he let the conversation serve its purpose: building natural friendliness. The right opportunity (perhaps her questions about the area or something in the news next week) will come, and then he can bring up the truth naturally on the next visit.

items.title: Following Up — Public Witnessing (lmd lesson 9 point 4)
items.answer:
lmd lesson 9 point 4 — “Think about the interested person. Based on your conversations with him, ask yourself: ‘Why does he need to hear the truth?’ ‘How would studying the Bible make his daily life and his future better?’”

PUBLIC WITNESSING — Daniel features a video from the Teaching Toolbox and offers a Bible study, shaping the offer around the person's real needs, exactly as the point directs. (In this demonstration he remembers Ruth from a previous call.)

Daniel (Publisher): "Good afternoon, Ruth. Do you remember me? Last month we spoke at your gate about the state of the world."
Ruth (Householder): "Ah yes! The one who said nobody is really in control."
Daniel (Publisher): "That's me. I didn't want to take your time then, but something you said stayed with me — you mentioned how hard it has become to make ends meet, and that you worry about your children's future."
Ruth (Householder): "Mmm, it's true. Sometimes I just feel tired of it all."
Daniel (Publisher): "I understand — many of us have felt that way. That's exactly why I'm here today. This short video shows how someone in a similar situation found real comfort from the Bible. May I play it for you? It takes about two minutes."
Ruth (Householder): "Okay, let me see."
Daniel (Publisher): (plays the video from the Teaching Toolbox)
Ruth (Householder): "Hmm. So the Bible really talks about people like me?"
Daniel (Publisher): "It does — and there's more. We arrange a free Bible study programme where you can ask your own questions and see what the Bible says about your worries — family, money, the future. Just one small portion a week, at a time that suits you. Would you like to try it?"
Ruth (Householder): "If it's free, why not? I like that it is short."
Daniel (Publisher): "Perfect. How about this same time next week — would that work?"

Keys: Daniel carries out lmd lesson 9 point 4 — he thought about Ruth beforehand: why she needs to hear the truth (worry and tiredness) and how a Bible study would make her daily life and her future better (real comfort, practical answers, hope). He listened, connected her needs to the video, and presented the study offer as the direct answer to her situation.

items.title: What Would You Say? — House to House (lmd lesson 1 point 4b)
items.answer: Discussion from the picture (mwb26 November p. 5). Briefly review lmd lesson 1 point 4b — be observant — then study the picture with the audience and discuss the two questions beneath it.
items.cite: mwb26 November p. 5 (picture) · lmd lesson 1 point 4b · John 5:28, 29

picture.alt: An apartment building hallway with three doors. One door is decorated with Christmas ornaments, a wreath, lights, and presents.
picture.cite: Life and Ministry Meeting Workbook, November 2026, p. 5 — wol.jw.org

pictureQuestions.label: Question 1
pictureQuestions.q: Based on what you observe, what question could you ask to start a conversation?
pictureQuestions.answer: Observation gives the opener. Looking at the decorated door — the wreath, the garland, the gifts — you could ask: 'Hello, these presents are beautiful — I guess your neighbours really spoil you at this time of year! What do you enjoy most about the season?' On the undecorated doors the observation is the opposite — and just as useful: 'Hi, you don't seem to be into all the holiday fuss on this floor — is that by choice?' Either way, the question flows from what you actually see, which is exactly what lesson 1 point 4b trains us to do: be observant before you speak.

pictureQuestions.label: Question 2
pictureQuestions.q: Which Bible truth might you share?
pictureQuestions.answer: A neighbour who pours so much love into family gifts cares deeply about family and about remembering loved ones — a natural bridge to the resurrection. Tell her that Jehovah treasures people just as she treasures her loved ones, and that his promise reaches further than any gift under a tree: a world where no family is ever torn apart by death, because those we have lost will come back. That hope can grow into a Bible study.

scriptures.quote: Do not be amazed at this, for the hour is coming in which all those in the memorial tombs will hear his voice and come out, those who did good things to a resurrection of life, and those who practiced vile things to a resurrection of judgment.

items.title: Do Not Forget Our Inactive Brothers and Sisters
items.answer:
Sample comment: "Ga 6:10 says we are to work what is good 'especially toward those related to us in the faith'—including those who have become inactive. The elders shepherd such ones willingly (1Pe 5:2), but each of us can help: send a warm card or text, invite them to a meal or family worship, offer practical help, and keep reaching out without judgment.

Expected lessons from the video 'Encourage the Inactive Ones' (to be confirmed after viewing): (1) reach out with warmth, not criticism; (2) small, consistent kindnesses stir a desire to return; (3) ordinary brothers and sisters, not only elders, share in this assistance."

scriptures.quote: So, then, as long as we have the opportunity, let us work what is good toward all, but especially toward those related to us in the faith.
Shepherd the flock of God under your care, serving as overseers, not under compulsion, but willingly before God; not for love of dishonest gain, but eagerly;

items.cite: Ga 6:10; 1Pe 5:2; video dramatization 'Encourage the Inactive Ones'

items.title: Congregation Bible Study — Walk Courageously With God, chap. 17
items.answer: Study source: the book Walk Courageously With God! (wcg), chapter 17, "Most Blessed of Women" — the account of Jael and Sisera (wcg chap. 17 pp. 82-85). The Bible account read: Judges 4:9, 11, 17-22; 5:24-31. Below are prepared answers to every question in the chapter — the discussion question, Dig Deeper, Reflect on the Lessons and Meditate on the Bigger Picture.

cbs.label: For discussion
cbs.q: In what ways did Jael show courage?
cbs.answer: Jael showed courage in several ways. She sided with Jehovah against a ruthless enemy even though her own husband had allied with that enemy's king. She faced a seasoned warrior alone — no soldier, no army, just a tent pin and a hammer. She knew that one slip, one false move, would cost her life. And she acted decisively at exactly the right moment, completing what Jehovah wanted done. Courage is not the absence of fear; it is choosing Jehovah's side and acting on it.

scriptures.quote: Jael the wife of Heber took a tent pin and a hammer in her hand. Then while he was fast asleep and exhausted, she stealthily approached him and drove the pin through his temples and beat it into the ground, and he died.

cbs.label: Dig Deeper · 1
cbs.q: What connection is there between the battle fought by Sisera and the battle of Armageddon? (w19.09 8-9 ¶3-6)
cbs.answer: Deborah's song places Israel's victory by the waters of Megiddo, where Jehovah Himself fought from the heavens. That battle pictures the coming war of Har-Magedon, when all the nations will gather against Jehovah's people — and the outcome will be the same. We are poorly armed by this world's standards, yet certain of victory, because the battle is not ours but God's. What He did at Megiddo, He will do again on a far greater scale.

scriptures.quote: Kings came, they fought; The kings of Canaan then fought In Taanach, by the waters of Megiddo. No spoil of silver did they take.
From heaven the stars fought; From their orbits they fought against Sisera.

cbs.label: Dig Deeper · 2
cbs.q: Jael's husband, Heber, allied himself with Israel's enemies the Canaanites. But how was Heber related to the Israelites? (it "Heber" No. 2)
cbs.answer: Heber was no foreigner — he was a Kenite, a descendant of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law. The Kenites had long been friendly with Israel and had even settled among them. That makes Heber's alliance with Canaanite King Jabin all the more sobering: he drifted away from the side of Jehovah's people. Jael, by contrast, held on to Jehovah's side. Family background saves no one — each one chooses whom he will support.

scriptures.quote: Incidentally, Heber the Kenite had separated from the Kenites, the descendants of Hobab, Moses' father-in-law, and his tent was pitched near the big tree in Zaanannim, which is at Kedesh.

cbs.label: Dig Deeper · 3
cbs.q: How did Israel's victory over Sisera and Jabin strengthen the faith of God's people many years later? (w08 10/15 14-15 ¶12-15)
cbs.answer: The victory was so complete that the land enjoyed rest, and Deborah's inspired song kept the memory alive for later generations. Whenever God's people afterwards faced overwhelming odds, they could reread how Jehovah scattered 900 iron chariots with an untrained army — and trust Him again. Faith is strengthened by remembering. When we face our own trials, rehearsing what Jehovah has already done for His people in the past steadies our hearts for what lies ahead.

scriptures.quote: So let all your enemies perish, O Jehovah, But let those who love you be like the sun rising in its glory. And the land had rest for 40 years.

cbs.label: Dig Deeper · 4
cbs.q: What is noteworthy about the way Deborah praised Jael? (w15 8/1 15 ¶3)
cbs.answer: Deborah praised Jael in words that became part of inspired Scripture: 'Most blessed of women is Jael.' Notice — Deborah, the judge and prophetess, did not keep the spotlight on herself. She honoured a humble woman who did what she could, and she gave all the glory to Jehovah for the victory. It teaches us to notice and praise faithful, quiet brothers and sisters who step forward courageously, however ordinary their role may look.

scriptures.quote: Most blessed of women is Jael, The wife of Heber the Kenite; She is most blessed of women living in tents.

cbs.label: Reflect · A
cbs.q: As Jael needed courage, when might a sister with an unbelieving husband need courage?
cbs.answer: When her husband opposes the meetings or mocks her hope, she needs courage to keep attending — sometimes alone. When he expects her to join in celebrations or practices that displease Jehovah, she needs courage to give a kind but firm answer. When he pressures her about money, work, or worldly connections, she needs courage to keep worship first. Like Jael, she quietly chooses Jehovah's side — not with a rebellious spirit, but with respectful, unshaken loyalty.

cbs.label: Reflect · B
cbs.q: Jael was not a prophetess like Deborah, nor was she a soldier like Barak. Still, she did what she could. What do we learn from her about how to view any limitations we might have?
cbs.answer: Jehovah used what was in Jael's hand — tools she used every day, and the courage she already had. She was not called to preach or command an army; she was called to act where she stood. It is the same with us. We may not be gifted speakers or appointed elders, but we can be hospitable, we can listen, we can teach a Bible study in simple words, we can support the congregation. Limitations do not excuse us — they simply shape what 'doing what we can' looks like.

cbs.label: Reflect · C
cbs.q: In what other ways might you imitate Jael's courage?
cbs.answer: Courage to identify openly with Jehovah's people when others around us stay neutral. Courage at school or at work to explain why we do not join certain activities. Courage to speak to a neighbour about Jehovah even when we feel shy. Courage to support our brothers in lands where the work is restricted — attending meetings, keeping our loyalty, never betraying our brothers. And courage to break free of any family or national alliance that conflicts with our worship, as Jael did.

cbs.label: Meditate · A
cbs.q: What does this account teach me about Jehovah?
cbs.answer: It teaches me that Jehovah is a God of justice who acts against ruthless oppressors, in His own time and His own way. It teaches me that what He foretells comes true exactly — Deborah said Sisera would fall by a woman's hand, and he did. It teaches me that Jehovah is not impressed by status: He chose a woman living in tents, with no army and no weapon worth the name, to deliver His people. Jehovah can be completely trusted to fight for those who take His side.

cbs.label: Meditate · B
cbs.q: How does the account tie in with Jehovah's purposes?
cbs.answer: Jehovah's victory over Sisera preserved His people and their worship, keeping the line through which the promised Seed would come. The battle by the waters of Megiddo foreshadows Har-Magedon, where Jehovah's appointed King, Jesus Christ, will complete the triumph and give mankind what that 40-year rest could only picture — true and lasting relief under Kingdom rule. Jael's courage, then, is part of a much bigger story: Jehovah will win, through whatever servants He chooses.

scriptures.quote: So let all your enemies perish, O Jehovah, But let those who love you be like the sun rising in its glory. And the land had rest for 40 years.

cbs.label: Meditate · C
cbs.q: What would I like to ask Jael in the resurrection?
cbs.answer: I would love to ask her: 'What went through your mind as you stood over that sleeping general — were you afraid? How did you gather the courage?' And also: 'What was it like to hear Deborah's song sung through the land, knowing your name was in it? Did you ever meet Deborah or Barak face to face?' I think she would smile and say the credit belonged to Jehovah all along.

wt.article: Sharing the Good News in “All the Languages of the Nations”

items.q: Why is it essential for the good news to be preached in many languages?
items.comment: It comes down to how salvation works. Paul asks a chain of questions: how can people call on Jehovah if they have not put faith in him? How can they put faith in someone they have never heard about? (Romans 10:13, 14). Ever since Babel, the human family has been split into language groups — so for anyone in that great crowd of Revelation 7:9 to call on Jehovah's name and be saved, the Kingdom message has to reach them in a language they truly understand. Preaching in many languages is not a side project; it is how salvation actually reaches them.

scriptures.quote: For “everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved.” However, how will they call on him if they have not put faith in him? How, in turn, will they put faith in him about whom they have not heard? How, in turn, will they hear without someone to preach?
scriptures.use: Paul explains that salvation depends on people hearing the good news from a preacher, so the message must be brought to them in a language they understand.

scriptures.quote: After this I saw, and look! a great crowd, which no man was able to number, out of all nations and tribes and peoples and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, dressed in white robes; and there were palm branches in their hands. ... These are the ones who come out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
scriptures.use: This shows that people from every language survive the great tribulation, which is possible only because the good news reached them in their own language.

scriptures.quote: So Jehovah scattered them from there over the entire face of the earth, and they gradually left off building the city. That is why it was named Baʹbel, because there Jehovah confused the language of all the earth, and Jehovah scattered them from there over the entire face of the earth.
scriptures.use: This explains how the human family was fragmented into language groups, creating the very language barrier the preaching work now overcomes.

items.insight: Salvation in Romans 10:13, 14 is a chain — calling, believing, hearing — and it breaks at the first missing link. The language work is not an add-on to the preaching work; for the great crowd it IS the preaching work.
items.apply: Check who in your territory speaks a different mother tongue, and prepare one tool in their language this week — even one video or tract in JW Library could be the first link in that chain.

paraNotes.points: Babel fragmented humanity into language groups, yet Jehovah purposes to unite a great crowd out of all nations and languages (Rev 7:9, ftn.). That crowd can call on his name only because the message reached them in their own language.
paraNotes.highlight: Romans 10:13, 14 is a chain of questions — each link depends on the one before it, and the last link is hearing in a language one understands.

items.q: What was the prophet Zechariah inspired to foretell?
items.comment: Zechariah foretold two things. First, that many nations would join themselves to Jehovah and become his people (Zech 2:11). Then the striking one: ten men out of all the languages of the nations taking firm hold of the robe of a Jew, saying: 'We want to go with you, for we have heard that God is with you people' (Zech 8:23). He wrote that some 2,600 years ago — and we are watching it come true. Let's see how each of us has a part in it.

scriptures.quote: Many nations will join themselves to Jehovah in that day, and they will become my people; and I will reside in your midst.
scriptures.use: This is the first part of Zechariah's foretell — that people of many nations would become Jehovah's people.

scriptures.quote: In those days ten men out of all the languages of the nations will take hold, yes, they will take firm hold of the robe of a Jew, saying: “We want to go with you, for we have heard that God is with you people.”
scriptures.use: This vividly pictures how people of all languages would eagerly join themselves to Jehovah's anointed people.

items.insight: Zechariah wrote to a small remnant rebuilding a temple, yet his prophecy reaches every language on earth. Jehovah's scope is always far bigger than the audience that first heard the words.
items.apply: When your territory feels small, remember the prophecy is worldwide — your street is one corner of a global fulfilment.

paraNotes.points: Zechariah foretold that many nations would join themselves to Jehovah (Zech 2:11) and that ten men out of all languages would take hold of the robe of a Jew (Zech 8:23).
paraNotes.highlight: The prophecy is being fulfilled in our day — this study shows how each one of us can have a share.

items.q: Who today are represented by the “Jew,” and who are represented by the “ten men”?
items.comment: The 'Jew' pictures anointed Christians — 'the Israel of God' — those with the heavenly calling (Gal 6:16; Heb 3:1). The 'ten men' picture the other sheep: humble ones from every nation and language who hope to live forever on a paradise earth. So the prophecy is not about ten literal men; it is about eager, teachable people of every background attaching themselves to Jehovah's anointed people so they can learn the way of worship.

scriptures.quote: As for all those who walk orderly by this rule of conduct, peace and mercy be upon them, yes, upon the Israel of God.
scriptures.use: Paul shows that the anointed ones are called ‘the Israel of God,’ identifying them as the ‘Jew’ of Zechariah's prophecy.

scriptures.quote: Consequently, holy brothers, partakers of the heavenly calling, consider the apostle and high priest whom we acknowledge—Jesus.
scriptures.use: This confirms that the anointed, the ‘Jew,’ are partakers of the heavenly calling.

items.insight: The picture echoes Ruth 1:16: 'your people will be my people.' The ten men do not merely visit — they cling. Attachment to Jehovah's people is how seekers become worshippers.
items.apply: If someone is 'taking hold' of you with sincere questions, do not just answer — attach them to the congregation: meetings, study, the family of worshippers.

paraNotes.points: The 'Jew' = anointed ones ('the Israel of God', Gal 6:16); the 'ten men' = humble ones of every linguistic and national background hoping for everlasting life on earth.
paraNotes.highlight: Holding the robe pictures attaching oneself to God's anointed people to be taught — the way Ruth clung to Naomi.

items.q: What happened after Jesus appointed “the faithful and discreet slave” in 1919?
items.comment: When Jesus appointed the faithful and discreet slave in 1919, that slave immediately understood the commission was international (Matt 24:45). The Photo-Drama of Creation had already reached international audiences; then came The Harp of God in 1921 — translated into 36 languages. And in 1935 the great crowd was clearly identified, revealing the enormous scope of the work. Within just two decades, Jehovah laid the foundation for a witnessing work that would reach all the languages of the nations.

scriptures.quote: Who really is the faithful and discreet slave whom his master appointed over his domestics, to give them their food at the proper time?
scriptures.use: This is the verse the paragraph cites to identify the slave appointed in 1919 and the spiritual food it provides to the domestics.

items.insight: Notice the rhythm: 1919 appointment, 1921 translation, 1935 scope revealed. Each step expanded exactly when the audience for it was identified — Jehovah prepares the workers for the harvest, and the harvest for the workers.
items.apply: The willing spirit of Psalm 110:3 is still the qualification that matters. Offer yourself for one language-related task this month — even small ones, like learning where the language tools live in JW Library.

paraNotes.points: After 1919 the slave organized international translation; The Harp of God (1921) reached 36 languages; 1935 identified the great crowd and the scale of the work ahead.
paraNotes.highlight: The heading quotes Psalm 110:3 — 'Your people will offer themselves willingly' — that willing spirit powered every step of the expansion.

items.q: How is Isaiah 2:2-4 being fulfilled today? (See also picture.)
items.comment: Isaiah foretold that people of all nations would stream to Jehovah's mountain to be instructed in his ways — and that is exactly what is happening (Isa 2:2-4). Righthearted ones are being found in every language group, and God's people have offered themselves willingly, not only to preach but to translate, print and ship the message (Ps 68:11; 110:3). Behind the scenes, programmers maintain JW Library and a multilanguage website. The result? Bible-based publications in over 1,100 languages — and every year, hundreds of thousands get baptized, many of them showing appreciation by donating to the worldwide work.

scriptures.quote: In the final part of the days, The mountain of the house of Jehovah Will become firmly established above the top of the mountains, And it will be raised up above the hills, And to it all the nations will stream. And many peoples will go and say: “Come, let us go up to the mountain of Jehovah, To the house of the God of Jacob. He will instruct us about his ways, And we will walk in his paths.” For law will go out of Zion, And the word of Jehovah out of Jerusalem. He will render judgment among the nations And set matters straight respecting many peoples. They will beat their swords into plowshares And their spears into pruning shears. Nation will not lift up sword against nation, Nor will they learn war anymore.
scriptures.use: This prophecy foretold that people from all nations would be invited to Jehovah’s house to be instructed about his ways — exactly what is happening through the preaching and translation work today.

scriptures.quote: Jehovah gives the command; The women proclaiming the good news are a large army.
scriptures.use: Shows that Jehovah has a large army of willing proclaimers, which matches the way God’s people today have offered themselves to preach and translate.

scriptures.quote: Your people will offer themselves willingly on the day of your military force.
scriptures.use: Directly quoted in paragraph 5 to show that God’s people willingly offer themselves to preach, translate, print, and ship the lifesaving message.

items.insight: Isaiah's 'mountain' is elevated worship — and the instruction happens IN the house of Jehovah, not just through a message. Donations are the quiet half of 'offering themselves willingly': the worldwide work runs on the voluntary support of worshippers in every language field.
items.apply: Invite an interested person to a meeting early in the conversation — instruction happens in the house — and carry one or two tools in the languages actually spoken on your territory.

paraNotes.points: Isa 2:2-4 is being fulfilled: people from all nations are invited to Jehovah's house and instructed in his ways; publishers, translators, printers and programmers all share in reaching them.
paraNotes.highlight: Look at the picture with these paragraphs — the multilingual preaching work in action.

paraNotes.points: Publications are available in over 1,100 languages; hundreds of thousands are baptized yearly; many show appreciation through voluntary donations.
paraNotes.highlight: Every one of those 1,100+ languages cost someone willing sacrifice — translators, printers, shippers, donors.

items.q: How are we affected by seeing the fulfillment of Revelation 14:6?
items.comment: Revelation 14:6 shows angels flying in midheaven, declaring everlasting good news to every nation, tribe, tongue and people — and today Jehovah's people, under angelic direction, are declaring it with tools that leap over language barriers. When we see Zechariah's and John's prophecies fulfilled right in front of us, it does two things: it makes us trust Bible prophecy, and it makes us cling to the organization God is using to proclaim the good news.

scriptures.quote: And I saw another angel flying in midheaven, and he had everlasting good news to declare to those who dwell on the earth, to every nation and tribe and tongue and people.
scriptures.use: This verse describes the angel-directed global preaching work, and its fulfillment today moves us to trust Bible prophecy and cling to God’s organization.

items.insight: Angels direct the preaching even where we cannot see it — the same message the angels declared is being declared by God's people under their direction. We are never working alone in the language fields.
items.apply: Before your service day, pray specifically for the language groups in your territory — the angels are already at work there.

paraNotes.points: Under angelic direction (Rev 14:6), God's people unitedly declare the everlasting good news to every nation, tribe, tongue and people with language-transcending tools.
paraNotes.highlight: Fulfilled prophecy builds trust — we cling all the more to the organization Jehovah is using.

items.q: At Pentecost 33 C.E., how did Jehovah reverse the effects of what he had done at the Tower of Babel?
items.comment: At Pentecost 33 C.E., Jehovah demonstrated that he can undo Babel: disciples miraculously spoke languages they had never learned, so that 'the magnificent things of God' reached an international crowd (Acts 2:4-11). There is no miraculous gift of tongues today — but in effect, our publications let us speak the language of the interested ones. When we hand someone a tract in their mother tongue, it is that same miracle in slow motion.

scriptures.quote: and they all became filled with holy spirit and started to speak in different languages, just as the spirit enabled them to speak.
scriptures.use: Shows that the disciples miraculously spoke languages they did not know, proving Jehovah could undo the language confusion of Babel.

scriptures.quote: Creʹtans, and Arabians—we hear them speaking in our languages about the magnificent things of God.”
scriptures.use: Gives the reason for the miracle: so the international crowd of God-fearing persons could hear the magnificent things of God in their own language.

items.insight: Pentecost was miraculous and temporary; today's 'tongues' are prepared tools — but the goal is identical: the magnificent things of God, heard in the hearer's language.
items.apply: Pick the one foreign language most common in your area and learn exactly where its tools live in JW Library — you will never be caught unprepared again.

paraNotes.points: Pentecost proved Jehovah can reverse Babel — the disciples spoke languages they did not know so God-fearing people could hear the magnificent things of God (Acts 2:4-11).
paraNotes.highlight: The reason for the miracle matters: the message had to be heard in the hearer's own language.

items.q: How can we help those who speak a language that we do not know to learn about the good news?
items.comment: The illustration in the article sticks with you: a traveller falls seriously ill overseas and cannot understand the doctor. Without an interpreter, the remedy that could save his life stays out of reach. Countless people are spiritually and emotionally sick today, and the remedy — the Bible's message — cannot help them in a language they cannot understand. Our tools — printed literature, videos, jw.org — are that interpreter. When we meet such a person, we can make sure the remedy arrives in a language he understands.
items.insight: The illustration turns a duty into a felt need: sick people do not need a lecture — they need the remedy in words they can understand. Language is the barrier, and we hold the interpreter.
items.apply: Find out from the elders or the territory map which migrant languages are actually spoken around you, and carry at least one tool in that language.

paraNotes.points: Illustration: a sick traveller needs an interpreter to understand the doctor's remedy — spiritually sick people need God's message in their own language.
paraNotes.highlight: The remedy already exists; the only thing standing between the person and the cure is language.

items.q: What do you learn from the experience of a brother named Robert and from the account in the box “A Refugee Finds Hope”?
items.comment: Robert's harbour-witnessing experience shows how simple this can be. He met a Turkish seaman with little English and gave him the brochure Good News From God! in Turkish. Because Robert knew the brochure's contents well, he guided the man to the right portions — then to the Bible's answers in Turkish on JW Library. The man was amazed: 'It is as if you knew my language!' After an hour's conversation his respect for the Bible had grown enormously. And Youa's story is just as moving — a Hmong refugee who hid one tract in her embroidery basket and read it secretly for years, until her daughter's Bible study finally brought her into full worship.
items.insight: Robert succeeded because he knew his brochure inside out — fluency in the CONTENT made the language handover work. And Youa's years of secret reading prove the seed keeps working long after we have left.
items.apply: Master one publication so well you could guide anyone through it in your own language — that mastery is what made Robert's conversation work.

paraNotes.points: Robert directed a Turkish-speaking seaman to portions of the brochure in his own language, then to the Bible's answers in Turkish on JW Library; the man's respect for the Bible rose sharply.
paraNotes.highlight: 'It is as if you knew my language!' — a person's heart language does what small talk never could.

paraNotes.points: Youa, a Hmong refugee, treasured one tract for years, reading it secretly in her embroidery basket, until a Bible study brought her into congregation worship.
paraNotes.highlight: Never underestimate a single tract in the right language — its seed can keep working for years after you leave.

items.q: What effect does reading and studying the New World Translation have on Jehovah’s people?
items.comment: All of us lean on the work of Bible translators — and translation is ancient: the Greek Septuagint was completed about 150 years before Christ. In our day the New World Translation has become a remarkable unifying tool — well over 300 languages, and the same clear, reliable message in every one of them. An elder serving in Nepal said reading it in his language made Jehovah more real to him and strengthened his faith. That is a big reason Jehovah's people can think and speak in agreement (1 Cor 1:10) — we are all literally reading the same Bible in every tongue.

scriptures.quote: Now I urge you, brothers, through the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you should all speak in agreement and that there should be no divisions among you, but that you may be completely united in the same mind and in the same line of thought.
scriptures.use: Paul's plea for unity is being fulfilled because Jehovah's people in over 300 languages read this clear, reliable translation that conveys the same message regardless of language.

items.insight: A common Bible does more than teach us — it binds us. 'Speak in agreement' is only possible when everyone reads the same clear translation in his own tongue.
items.apply: Read one passage this week in two languages and notice the unity of the message — then show that feature to an interested person.

paraNotes.points: The New World Translation, available whole or in part in over 300 languages, unifies Jehovah's people — the same message regardless of language (1 Cor 1:10).
paraNotes.highlight: Footnote a: the first Bible translation, the Greek Septuagint, was completed about 150 B.C.E. And the elder in Nepal said the translation made Jehovah 'more real' to him.

items.q: Why do few modern Bible translations use God’s name?
items.comment: The New World Translation is one of the very few Bibles distributed in this century that still honours Jehovah's name throughout its text. It was not always so rare — in the early last days many translations carried the name, especially in the Hebrew Scriptures. But Christendom's leaders have grown increasingly hostile to it: the Catholic Church removed it from its Bibles and literature, and most Protestant denominations leave it out too. Our translation goes the other way — restoring the divine name to its rightful place, in every language.
items.insight: Omitting the name is not neutral scholarship — it fits the propaganda that God is unknowable. Restoring it in over 300 languages is part of making his name known before the nations.
items.apply: When talking with a churchgoer, show the name in their own Bible's Hebrew Scriptures where it still appears, or in our appendix — it opens honest conversation.

paraNotes.points: Most modern translations omit the divine name; the New World Translation restores it consistently regardless of language.
paraNotes.highlight: Footnote b: in 2008 Pope Benedict XVI directed that God's name is 'neither to be used nor pronounced' in Catholic services, hymns or prayers.

items.q: According to the Scriptures, why is it important to know and to use God's name?
items.comment: Using God's name is not a small doctrinal detail — Scripture makes it essential. The psalmist urges God's servants to praise the name of Jehovah (Ps 135:1). Jesus taught us to pray, 'Let your name be sanctified' (Matt 6:9), and said near his death, 'I have made your name known' (John 17:26). Paul quotes Joel: 'Everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved' (Rom 10:13). People whose Bibles leave the name out simply cannot obey those inspired commands. That is why our translation's faithfulness matters so much.

scriptures.quote: Praise the name of Jehovah; Offer praise, you servants of Jehovah,
scriptures.use: Shows that God's servants are urged to praise the name of Jehovah.

scriptures.quote: Our Father in the heavens, let your name be sanctified.
scriptures.use: Records Jesus directing his disciples to pray that God's name be sanctified.

scriptures.quote: I have made your name known to them and will make it known, so that the love with which you loved me may be in them and I in union with them.
scriptures.use: Shows that Jesus made his Father's name known and promised to keep making it known.

scriptures.quote: For “everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved.”
scriptures.use: Explains that salvation depends on calling on the name of Jehovah.

items.insight: The name is woven through the whole Christian life — praised, sanctified in prayer, made known, called upon for salvation. A Bible without the name cuts the believer off from all four.
items.apply: Use Jehovah's name naturally this week — in prayer and in conversation — not awkwardly, but the way family speaks about someone they love.

paraNotes.points: Scripture commands knowing and using the name — Ps 135:1; Matt 6:9; John 17:26; Rom 10:13. Those using nameless Bibles cannot obey these exhortations.
paraNotes.highlight: Sanctifying the name is the very first request in the model prayer.

items.q: How do Jehovah's people feel about the divine name?
items.comment: Because most of us hold a translation that faithfully carries the name, we have grown to love it and to rely on the One it represents. 'The name of Jehovah is a strong tower; the righteous one runs into it and is protected' (Prov 18:10). And anyone — from any nation, any tongue — is welcome to run into that tower with us: foreigners who join themselves to Jehovah find refuge there too (Isa 56:6).

scriptures.quote: The name of Jehovah is a strong tower. Into it the righteous one runs and receives protection.
scriptures.use: Illustrates that Jehovah's name is a strong tower where the righteous one finds protection, showing why we rely on it.

scriptures.quote: As for the foreigners who join themselves to Jehovah to minister to him, To love the name of Jehovah And to be his servants, All those who keep the Sabbath and do not profane it And who hold fast to my covenant,
scriptures.use: Shows that those who join themselves to Jehovah learn to love his name and serve him.

items.insight: Isaiah 56:6 already pictured what Zechariah 8:23 predicts: seekers of every nation attaching themselves to God's people. The tower has always been open to foreigners.
items.apply: Make newcomers who are still learning the local language feel the congregation is their tower too — a simple welcome in their language goes far.

paraNotes.points: Jehovah's people love and rely on the name — a strong tower (Prov 18:10); foreigners who join themselves to Jehovah are welcomed to it (Isa 56:6).
paraNotes.highlight: The tower picture: protection belongs to everyone who runs to it, whatever their language.

items.q: Why is it urgent to come to know Jehovah now? (John 17:3)
items.comment: The Bible foretells a showdown in the near future between the kings of the entire inhabited earth and Jehovah (Rev 16:14). In that war, those who know Jehovah will be kept safe — 'those knowing your name will trust in you' (Ps 9:10) — and Jesus said that knowing the only true God means everlasting life (John 17:3). But those who refuse to know him as Father will come to know him a different way: 'they will have to know that I am Jehovah' (Ezek 38:23). How happy we are to know him as a Friend now, not as an adversary then!

scriptures.quote: They are, in fact, expressions inspired by demons and they perform signs, and they go out to the kings of the entire inhabited earth, to gather them together to the war of the great day of God the Almighty.
scriptures.use: Foretells the gathering of the kings of the entire inhabited earth to the war of the great day of God, the showdown Jehovah's people must survive.

scriptures.quote: Those knowing your name will trust in you; You will never abandon those seeking you, O Jehovah.
scriptures.use: Promises that those who know Jehovah and honor his name will be kept safe.

scriptures.quote: This means everlasting life, their coming to know you, the only true God, and the one whom you sent, Jesus Christ.
scriptures.use: Shows that coming to know the only true God is the way to everlasting life, making it urgent to know him now.

scriptures.quote: And I will certainly magnify myself and sanctify myself and make myself known before the eyes of many nations; and they will have to know that I am Jehovah.’
scriptures.use: Warns that those who refuse to know Jehovah as their Father will be forced to know him in a different way.

scriptures.quote: At that time those who fear Jehovah spoke with one another, each one with his companion, and Jehovah kept paying attention and listening. And a book of remembrance was written before him for those fearing Jehovah and for those meditating on his name.
scriptures.use: Shows that Jehovah pays attention to those who fear him and meditate on his name, and they will rejoice to know him as their Friend.

items.insight: In the end everyone will know Jehovah — the question is whether as Friend or as adversary. The great crowd survives because it called on the name it came to know in its own language.
items.apply: Ask yourself honestly: am I deepening that friendship now, while it is still a friendship?

paraNotes.points: Armageddon is the ultimate 'knowing' — those who know Jehovah are kept safe (Ps 9:10; John 17:3); his enemies will be forced to know who he is (Ezek 38:23).
paraNotes.highlight: The study note on John 17:3: 'coming to know you' means an intimate, ongoing relationship — not just facts.

items.comment: So what a privilege we have — playing even a small role in the fulfilment of Zechariah 8:23! We work unitedly not only with our brothers and sisters but with the angels in this multilingual preaching work. Jehovah keeps giving us the tools to reach every nation and tongue; our part is to use them well, drawing as many as possible to our impartial, merciful and patient God. It is our honour to keep at this work until Jehovah's name is sanctified before all creation (Luke 11:2).

scriptures.quote: “This is what Jehovah of armies says, ‘In those days ten men out of all the languages of the nations will take hold, yes, they will take firm hold of the robe of a Jew, saying: “We want to go with you, for we have heard that God is with you people.”’”
scriptures.use: Is the prophecy we share in fulfilling today as humble ones from all languages take hold of the robe of the anointed ones.

scriptures.quote: So he said to them: “Whenever you pray, say: ‘Father, let your name be sanctified. Let your Kingdom come.
scriptures.use: Reminds us that sanctifying God's name is the goal of our preaching work and of our prayers.

items.insight: The article ends where the model prayer begins. The multilingual preaching work is our own prayer — 'let your name be sanctified' — in progress.
items.apply: Keep praying for the name to be sanctified — and watch for the part you personally can play in its fulfilment this month.

paraNotes.points: We work with the angels in the multilingual preaching work, using Jehovah's tools to draw people to him until his name is sanctified.
paraNotes.highlight: The conclusion loops back to the model prayer — 'let your name be sanctified' (Luke 11:2). The whole article rides on that one request.

recap.q: Who are represented by the “Jew” and by the “ten men” mentioned at Zechariah 8:23?
recap.comment: The “Jew” represents those whom God has anointed with holy spirit — “the Israel of God” — who have the heavenly calling. The “ten men” represent humble ones who hope to live forever in Paradise on earth, from all linguistic and national backgrounds. Today they eagerly take hold of the robe of the anointed, asking to learn about God.

recap.q: What is making it possible for people from every tongue to learn about Jehovah?
recap.comment: The faithful and discreet slave recognized that its commission was international in scope. Willing volunteers preach, translate, print, and ship publications in over 1,100 languages, the New World Translation is available in well over 300 languages, and tools such as JW Library and the jw.org website help us reach people in the language of their heart.

recap.q: Why is it important for people to know and to use Jehovah's name?
recap.comment: Because everyone who calls on the name of Jehovah will be saved. Jesus taught us to pray that God's name be sanctified, and knowing the only true God means everlasting life. Those using translations that omit the divine name cannot obey these exhortations, and those refusing to know Jehovah will be forced to know him in a different way.

daily.scripture: Commit to Jehovah whatever you do.​
daily.comment: As the present system of things draws closer to its end, we can expect economic conditions to worsen. Political turmoil, armed conflicts, natural disasters, or new pandemics might lead to unexpected expenses or to the loss of our job, our possessions, or our home. What can help us to make decisions that show our trust in Jehovah’s hand? A primary and effective step is to take your concerns to Jehovah. Ask him for the wisdom you need to make good decisions and for a calm heart to avoid “being in anxious suspense” about your situation. ( Luke 12:29-31 ) Petition him to help you cultivate contentment with life’s necessities. ( 1 Tim. 6:7, 8 ) Do research in our publications on how to deal successfully with financial problems. Many have benefited from material available on jw.org that deals with economic problems. w25.03 28-29 ¶10-11 November 16-22

daily.scripture: God has shown me that I should call no man defiled or unclean.​
daily.comment: The time had arrived for uncircumcised Gentiles to become part of God’s people. The apostle Peter was assigned to preach to the Gentile Cornelius, who would be among the first of this new group of worshippers. Jews had very little to do with Gentiles, so it is not surprising that Peter needed help to prepare for his assignment. When Peter discerned God’s will in this matter, he adjusted his viewpoint. As a result, when he was sent for, he went “without objection.” ( Acts 10:28, 29 ) He preached to Cornelius and his household, and they got baptized. ( Acts 10:21-23, 34, 35, 44-48 ) Years later, Peter encouraged fellow Christians to “think in agreement.” ( 1 Pet. 3:8 , ftn.) As Jehovah’s people, we can think in agreement by reflecting Jehovah’s thinking as it is expressed in his Word. w25.03 9-10 ¶7-8 November 16-22

daily.scripture: Do not be led astray by various and strange teachings.​
daily.comment: The attitudes and opinions of the world are becoming ever more distant from God’s perfect view of matters. ( Prov. 17:15 ) We, therefore, must strengthen our ability to identify and reject ideas that opposers use in an attempt to discourage us or even to lead us astray. We do well to take to heart the counsel that the apostle Paul gave the Hebrew Christians, to press on to spiritual maturity. That includes acquiring a deep knowledge of the truth and adopting Jehovah’s way of thinking. This process continues even after dedication and baptism. No matter how long we have been in the truth, all of us must regularly read and study God’s Word. ( Ps. 1:2 ) A good routine of personal study will help us to strengthen a quality that Paul emphasized in his letter to the Hebrews: faith.​— Heb. 11:1, 6 . w24.09 10 ¶7-8 November 16-22

daily.scripture: Draw close to God, and he will draw close to you.​
daily.comment: If Jehovah is real to us, we will find it easier to stay faithful to him. That was true of Joseph. He firmly refused to commit immorality. God was real to him, and he didn’t want to displease Him. ( Gen. 39:9 ) For Jehovah to be real to us, we need to make time to pray to him and to study his Word. Our friendship with him will thus grow. When, like Joseph, we have a close friendship with Jehovah, we will not want to do anything that displeases Him. Those who forget that Jehovah is the living God can easily draw away from him. Consider what happened to the Israelites when they were in the wilderness. They were aware that Jehovah existed, but they began to doubt that he would provide for them. ( Ex. 17:2, 7 ) Thereafter, they rebelled against God. Surely, we want to avoid following their disobedient course, which stands as a warning example for us.​— Heb. 3:12 . w24.06 24 ¶14-15 November 16-22

daily.scripture: The eyes of Jehovah are on the righteous, and his ears listen to their cry for help.​
daily.comment: We are living deep in the last days, and we expect that causes of tears will only increase. Jehovah sees the tears we shed and is deeply moved by them. Our tears are truly precious to him. So when we face distressing situations, we certainly want to pour out our heart to Jehovah in prayer. May we never isolate ourselves from our loving brothers and sisters in the congregation. And may we continue to find comfort in the soothing words recorded in the Bible. We can be sure that if we keep enduring faithfully, Jehovah will reward us. That includes the wonderful promise that in time he will wipe out every tear of sorrow, betrayal, and despair from our eyes. ( Rev. 21:4 ) Then we will shed only tears of joy. w24.12 20 ¶3; 25 ¶19 November 16-22

Jehovah has appointed us to be his Witnesses, and he promises to help us be courageous. ( Isa. 43:10, 11 ) Consider just four of the ways he does that. First, Jesus is with us whenever we preach the good news. ( Matt. 28:18-20 ) Second, Jehovah has appointed angels to help us. ( Rev. 14:6 ) Third, Jehovah has given us his holy spirit as a helper to bring back to our minds the things we have learned. ( John 14:25, 26 ) Fourth, Jehovah has provided brothers and sisters to accompany us. With Jehovah’s backing and the support of our loving brotherhood, we have everything we need to be successful. But if you feel discouraged when you find few people at home, ask yourself: ‘Where are the people from my territory right now?’ ( Acts 16:13 ) ‘Are they at work or out shopping?’ If that is the case, could you find more people by doing street witnessing? w24.04 17 ¶10-11 November 16-22

daily.scripture: If any man does not know how to preside over his own household, how will he care for the congregation of God?​
daily.comment: If you are a husband and want to qualify as an elder, the reputation of your family will affect your qualifications. Thus, you need to be “presiding over [your] own household in a fine manner.” You need to have a reputation for being a loving and responsible family head. This includes taking the lead in all aspects of our worship. If you are a father, you must have your minor “children in subjection with all seriousness.” ( 1 Tim. 3:4 ) You need to teach and train them lovingly. Of course, like all children, they will enjoy laughing and playing. But because of your good training, they will be obedient, respectful, and well-behaved. Also, you must do your best to help your children to develop a good relationship with Jehovah, to live by Bible principles, and to progress to baptism. w24.11 22 ¶10-11 November 16-22
